title: SO3LR Tauri: Generally Applicable Force Fields for Reactive (Bio)Molecular Simulations Covering the Periodic Table
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06237v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Machine-learned force fields (MLFFs) aim to create a unified model that describes all major classes of (bio)molecules at quantum-mechanical accuracy. We present SO3LR Tauri, a family of MLFFs developed toward this goal, coupling a fast SO3krates network to explicit, physics-based interaction modules: pair-specific short-range repulsion, environment-dependent dispersion, and electrostatics, each improved beyond its original formulation. The models are trained on 148 million structures spanning 85 elements, drawn from several quantum-chemical datasets. Against coupled-cluster references, the models accurately reproduce nucleobase-pair and charged protein-ligand interactions, carbohydrate conformer ordering, and molecular dipoles. They also resolve the transition pathways of organic and enzymatic reactions. Dynamical simulations recover experimental densities of water and organic solvents, the hydration structure of mono- and divalent ions, the pKa values of amino-acid side chains, and the structure and dynamics of proteins, membranes, nucleic acids, glycoproteins, and metal-containing biomolecules, all without system-specific fitting. Released in three sizes, the models reach 0.7-3.2 $\mu$s/atom and scale to 27-84 million atoms on a single GPU. Much work remains to be done: achieving predictive accuracy for static and dynamic liquid properties, reaction barriers, coverage of chemical and conformational space, and the sampling and inference speed needed to describe biomolecular processes.
relevance_reason: Key author: Klaus-Robert M\"{u}ller, Alexandre Tkatchenko

title: A Machine Learning Model for the Chemistry of a Solvated Electron
abstract:
arXiv:2511.22642v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: In molecular simulations, machine-learning force fields can achieve ab initio accuracy at a lower cost but remain limited in the explicit modeling of electrons. In this work, we develop an electron-aware machine-learning force field, in which an excess electron of interest is modeled quantum mechanically, while the remaining short-range interactions and long-range Coulombic forces are machine-learned to reproduce a density functional theory calculation. We demonstrate the method on the solvated electron in bulk water and its reaction with a hydronium ion. We identify a proton transfer mechanism by which the excess proton recombines with the electron. We determine the forward reaction rates between 350 K and 450 K from first-passage survival functions, which yield an Arrhenius relationship with an activation energy of 3.2 kcal$\cdot$mol$^{-1}$, in good agreement with experiment. From an enhanced sampling simulation, we determine the equilibrium constant, and thus the reaction free energy, which is also consistent with experimental measurements.
relevance_reason: Key author: Roberto Car

title: Quantitatively Probing the Tilt Angle Failures in 4D-STEM Polarisation Analysis
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06274v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) is increasingly used to map polarisation in ferroic textures such as domain walls, vortices, merons and skyrmions. These textures are accompanied by local strain, lattice rotation and misorientation, which also modulate the diffraction features used to infer polar order. Even small deviations from the zone axis can therefore produce contrast that is indistinguishable from a polarisation signal. Here we quantify the tilt sensitivity of two polarisation-sensitive signals, diffraction disc intensity and Kikuchi band intensity, in three ferroelectrics with distinct polar distortions: PbTiO3, BaTiO3 and Cu3B7O13Cl boracite. We find that tilts of only 0.01-0.05 degrees reverse most Friedel-pair disc asymmetries, and even the most robust disc pairs reverse by 0.04 degrees in BaTiO3, 0.14 degrees in PbTiO3 and 0.18 degrees in boracite, producing contrast equal and opposite to that of the polarisation. Kikuchi band contrast is the only signal that reports absolute polarity without knowledge of the specimen thickness, but it does so only up to 0.09 degrees in PbTiO3, 0.015 degrees in BaTiO3 and 0.02 degrees in boracite. From these results we define tilt tolerances for each signal and material, and propose practical criteria for distinguishing polarisation contrast from misorientation. The analysis also applies to scanning electron microscopy-based diffraction, including electron backscatter diffraction.
relevance_reason: Key author: Aron Walsh

title: Excited-state intramolecular proton transfer dynamics with neural network potentials and nuclear quantum effects
abstract: Excited-state intramolecular proton transfer is a prototypical ultrafast process that forms the foundation for many chemical and biological phenomena and is highly sensitive to changes in the underlying potential energy landscape. Here, we develop neural network potentials for 10-hydroxybenzo[h]quinoline that describe ground- and excited-state dynamics with near ab initio accuracy. These neural network potentials enable efficient sampling of the proton transfer coordinate and incorporation of nuclear quantum effects through path-integral molecular dynamics. The free energy profiles show that excited-state intramolecular proton transfer proceeds on a largely barrierless excited-state surface, with nuclear quantum effects reducing and smoothing the residual barrier. Non-equilibrium simulations yield an average proton transfer time of ∼11.5 fs for quantum hydrogen, consistent with experiment, and reveal a clear isotope effect, with slower dynamics for deuterium and classical nuclei. Mechanistic analysis identifies transient proton donor–acceptor contraction as the key enabling coordinate, while the proton crosses the midpoint prior to reaching the minimum of this coordinate, indicating a dynamically driven transfer. Subtle changes in the conjugated backbone precede proton transfer, reflecting early electronic reorganization and coherent coupling between proton motion and backbone vibrations. Bond-length alternation and vibrational coherence analysis reveal isotope-dependent coherence loss, with deuteration producing stronger damping and more localized proton/backbone dynamics relative to hydrogen. These results establish neural network potential-based approaches as an effective framework for simulating excited-state proton transfer with explicit nuclear quantum effects.
relevance_reason: Develops neural network potentials for ground- and excited-state dynamics and uses path-integral MD plus free-energy/non-equilibrium simulations, strongly satisfying (a), (b), and (c).

title: Exact periodic electrostatics for latent-charge machine-learning potentials
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06575v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials of the latent Ewald summation (LES) type learn atomic charges from energies and forces and evaluate their electrostatic energy in reciprocal space. I formulate this long-range term as a smeared Epstein-Hurwitz lattice sum and derive its exact periodic structure: a decomposition isolating a net-charge artefact and a local self-energy, an image theorem for cells of any shape, and the forces and virial. Full charge equilibration, LES with induced charges, constrained and unconstrained LES models and fixed-charge force fields follow as successive approximations of one variational problem, whose diagonal-hardness limit is a projection of the latent charges onto fixed total charge, which I call projected latent Ewald summation (pLES). Energies and forces determine the latent charges only up to a gauge, so fragment-level rather than atom-level charge quantization is the consistent target. The latent channel is guaranteed to be a dielectric only if charge is conserved locally; charges that are local functions of the environment and conserved only globally can screen like a conductor. pLES is implemented in the atomic cluster expansion and in LAMMPS, and the exact identities hold to machine precision, also for trained models. For charged NaCl clusters, pLES recovers the total charge that an unconstrained model misses by up to 1.8 e and reduces the test errors of a short-range model from 1.44 to 0.42 meV/atom and from 37 to 13 meV/{\AA}. In two water datasets, constrained and unconstrained models learn the same latent charges up to sign and scale. In molecular dynamics of pLES water, fluctuating molecular charges dominate the screening at all accessible wavelengths; a crossover model excludes a conductor and gives a latent dielectric constant between 19 and 71; molecular charges are compensated over about 1 nm, beyond the training cells.
relevance_reason: Derives exact periodic electrostatics for latent-Ewald machine-learned interatomic potentials and implements it in ACE and LAMMPS, validating energies/forces on charged NaCl clusters, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) MLIP/force-field development with Ewald methods, and (c) methodological advance.

title: Machine-Learning-Accelerated Metallene Stabilization from High-Throughput Sandwich Modeling
abstract:
arXiv:2608.01779v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Metallenes have appealing properties, but stabilizing them in a monolayer phase poses synthesis challenges. A recent experiment showed that the van der Waals squeezing method can stabilize certain metallenes in a MoS2 sandwich. This pioneering work motivates systematic studies, but such studies are experimentally impractical, while first-principles modeling remains prohibitive. Here, using universal machine-learning interatomic potentials, we constructed 1620 metallene sandwich heterostructures containing 6 different sandwich layers and 45 metals. We performed phonon calculations, which revealed 1208 dynamically stable structures and narrowed them to 331 after structural filtering. We found that Se-based transition-metal dichalcogenides stabilize metallenes effectively. Specifically, hexagonal and buckled hexagonal crystal lattices exhibit the greatest stability. We further evaluated the thermal stability of selected heterostructures with density-functional theory molecular dynamics simulations at room temperature. By uncovering the physical and chemical factors that govern metallenes stabilization, our results provide systematic insights to guide and accelerate synthesis for future applications.
relevance_reason: Uses universal machine-learning interatomic potentials to build and screen 1620 metallene sandwich heterostructures with phonon calculations and DFT molecular dynamics validation, clearly satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) MLIP/DFT-MD methodology, and (c) applied materials discovery.

title: Subtle Energy Corrections Reshape Condensed-Phase Property Predictions from a Machine-Learning Interatomic Potential
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06109v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Accurate reproduction of electronic-structure labels by machine-learning interatomic potentials does not necessarily ensure reliable condensed-phase properties. We investigate the effects of basis-set superposition error (BSSE) and an explicit Axilrod-Teller-Muto (ATM) three-body dispersion contribution on molecular-liquid predictions. Starting from MACELES-OFF, we fine-tune a baseline potential at the $\omega$B97M-V/def2-TZVPD level. A separate branch learns counterpoise (CP) energy and force corrections with the baseline frozen, while a D4-parametrized ATM term is added during molecular-dynamics inference. Mean atom-normalized CP and ATM contributions are 0.222 and 0.205 meV/atom, respectively, for the analyzed SPICE2 configurations from OMol25. We compare baseline, CP-only, ATM-only, and CP + ATM variants for 39 organic liquids. Relative to baseline, the mean system-wise density changes are -1.17%, -10.38%, and -11.93% for CP-only, ATM-only, and CP + ATM, respectively; the corresponding enthalpy-of-vaporization changes are -2.79%, -14.74%, and -18.32%. For the 11 liquids with experimental self-diffusion data, the mean self-diffusion changes are +17.66%, +203.02%, and +230.36%. Both corrections thus lower density and enthalpy of vaporization while increasing molecular mobility on average. ATM dominates these changes, while CP provides a smaller contribution; their combination yields the largest average shifts. These results show that corrections with sub-meV/atom mean values on the analyzed configurations can substantially reshape the predicted structural, thermodynamic, and transport properties of molecular liquids.
relevance_reason: Fine-tunes and corrects a machine-learned interatomic potential (MACELES-OFF) with BSSE/Axilrod-Teller-Muto terms and runs MD on 39 organic liquids to compute densities, enthalpies of vaporization and diffusion, so (a) explicit atoms, (b) MLIP development plus classical MD, and (c) method/transferability advance are all satisfied.

title: Shock-driven Jetting at HMX Crystal Surface Asperities
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05752v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Shock-induced jetting and recompression are plausible mechanisms for hot spot formation in energetic materials, but remain poorly understood. To this end, we apply all-atom nonreactive molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of a shock-loaded sinusoidal surface asperity in the crystalline explosive HMX (octahydro-1,3,5,7-tetranitro-1,3,5,7-tetrazocine) to quantify the roles of shock strength, asperity geometry, system size, and crystallographic orientation in determining the jetting response. Our simulations span a shock pressure interval of $\approx$4-47 GPa, which captures responses in both detonation initiation and steady-state detonation regimes. We find that shock strength and asperity curvature exert strong influence on jet velocity, temperature, and morphology, while feature size and crystallographic orientation play more modest roles. Jet morphology correlates strongly with the HMX ambient-pressure phase diagram and the narrow temperature range associated with its liquid phase. Coherent jets form when focusing and dissipation are sufficient to drive local temperatures above the melting point, while formation of molecular plumes is seemingly connected to jet temperatures exceeding the liquid-vapor transition temperature. Formation of plumes is unlike the jetting responses seen in metals, which typically exhibit liquid phases that are stable over wider temperature intervals. This work proposes a simple hypothesis for the connection between jet morphology and ambient-pressure phase diagrams that can be readily tested in other explosives and metals. It also provides a foundation for ongoing nonreactive and reactive MD simulations of jet impact and recompression to quantify the role played by jets in forming hot spots in HMX-based explosives.
relevance_reason: All-atom nonreactive molecular dynamics simulations of shock-loaded HMX surface asperities quantify jetting and hot-spot mechanisms, clearly satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) classical MD, and (c) application to learn shock-induced chemistry physics.

title: Temperature-Dependent Ion Dynamics in Argyrodite Superionic Conductor Li$_{6}$PS$_{5}$Cl with Fine-Tuned MACE Foundation Model
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05946v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The rapid growth of machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIP), particularly the foundational models for materials chemistry, such as MACE, has significantly strengthened our capabilities in studying the complex dynamics of materials through statistical sampling. Here, by performing molecular dynamics with a fine-tuned MACE model, that are further combined with essential dynamics analysis, a tool that is commonly applied in (bio)molecular simulations, we examine the temperature-dependent ion dynamics in a prototypical inorganic solid superionic conductor, namely argyrodite Li$_{6}$PS$_{5}$Cl. Our analyses show clear localised phonon-like dynamics for Li$^+$ ions below 500 K with trajectories lying in a low-dimensional manifold that is highly nonlinear, which is opposite to the case in the high-temperature ($\sim$800 K) end. Between 500-700 K, the system exhibit strong competition in the dynamics between the Li$^+$ and framework ions, that are reflected in both the eigenspectrum and the projected low-dimensional embeddings characterising these dynamics not showing a simple monotonic dependency upon rising temperatures, and is further supported by investigations employing Langevin dynamics that systematically examine how damping the framework motions affects the dynamics of the Li$^+$ ions, thanks to the computational efficiency provided by MLIP. This work thus contributes towards the broader theoretical and data-driven framework for studying the lattice dynamics of solids.
relevance_reason: Fine-tunes and runs the MACE machine-learned interatomic potential to perform MD of Li6PS5Cl, directly satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) MLIP development/application with MD, and (c) learning about temperature-dependent ion dynamics.

title: An All-Atom Model of the Resorcinol-Formaldehyde Aerogel Skeleton from DFT and Molecular Dynamics: Validation and Iron Incorporation
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06277v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Resorcinol-formaldehyde (RF) aerogels are lightweight, ultra-porous thermal superinsulators whose complex amorphous structure has not yet been described at the all-atom level. Here, we build an all-atom model of the RF aerogel skeleton by combining density functional theory (DFT) and classical molecular dynamics (MD), validate it against experimental infrared and density measurements, and use it to study the incorporation of iron dopants. The RF base unit was optimized with Gaussian, DMol$^{3}$ and SIESTA, and its calculated infrared spectrum agreed with experiment. Comparing classical force fields with DFT for branched systems of two to four base units (140-278 atoms) led to the choice of COMPASS II. A 15,012-atom system of 54 branched RF units, not cross-linked to each other, aggregated into a single cluster in the canonical (NVT) ensemble and reached an equilibrium density of 1.296 g.cm$^{-3}$ in the isobaric-isothermal (NPT) ensemble, in agreement with the experimental skeletal density (1.3 g.cm$^{-3}$). Then, 5 wt$\%$ iron (109 atoms) was added to the equilibrated structure: during 1 ns of NPT simulation, the fraction of iron atoms embedded in the skeleton rose from 63$\%$ to 71$\%$, and the Fe-C radial distribution function peaked at 3 \AA. The model thus provides an experimentally supported starting point for screening fillers and dopants in RF gels, with prospective application to their thermoelectric functionalization, which we have previously demonstrated experimentally with basalt and PANOX fibres. Future extensions could address skeleton properties relevant to thermal insulation and the pyrolysis of RF gels into carbon and metal-doped carbon aerogels.
relevance_reason: Builds an all-atom aerogel model using DFT and classical MD (COMPASS II force field benchmarking and NVT/NPT simulations of 15k atoms), satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) force-field comparison plus MD, and (c) application to structure and dopant incorporation.

title: Cancer-associated histone tail mutations reshape conformational ensembles and DNA-contact states in nucleosomes
abstract: Cancer-associated histone mutations can perturb chromatin regulation, yet how many noncanonical mutations in intrinsically disordered histone tails alter nucleosome dynamics remains poorly understood. Here, we combine pan-cancer histone mutation profiling with 31.5 μs of all-atom molecular dynamics simulations of complete nucleosomes to investigate recurrent mutations in the H2A, H2B, H3, and H4 tails. We identify recurrent and understudied mutation sites beyond canonical H3 oncohistones and characterize how selected substitutions perturb histone-tail conformational ensembles and DNA contacts in their nucleosomal context. The simulations reveal mutation-specific redistribution of tail–DNA contacts across the nucleosomal DNA surface, accompanied by changes in MM/GBSA-derived relative interaction-energy estimates. For selected systems, Markov state modeling further resolves metastable tail–DNA contact states and shows that mutations alter their structural characteristics and population distributions. These perturbations are not confined to the substituted residues but extend to neighboring interaction networks. Together, our results provide a molecular-level physical picture of how cancer-associated histone-tail mutations reshape conformational and interaction-state landscapes in nucleosomes.
relevance_reason: 31.5 μs all-atom molecular dynamics of nucleosomes with MM/GBSA and Markov state modeling; explicit atoms, MD/free-energy analysis, and biological application satisfy (a)-(c).

title: The effects of the substrate and graphene on the interfacial structures of DMSO revealed by heterodyne-detected sum frequency generation (HD-SFG) spectroscopy and molecular dynamics analysis
abstract: Understanding molecular structures at electrode/electrolyte interfaces is essential for optimizing high-performance electrochemical reactions. Here, we investigated the interfacial structures of dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), a widely used aprotic solvent, at the air/DMSO, SiO2/DMSO, and air/graphene/DMSO interfaces by heterodyne-detected sum frequency generation (HD-SFG) spectroscopy and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. HD-SFG spectroscopy is an interface-selective nonlinear spectroscopic technique capable of determining the absolute orientation of interfacial molecules. To enable HD-SFG measurements at the buried SiO2/DMSO interface, where precise optical phase control is challenging, an octadecyltrichlorosilane self-assembled monolayer was introduced on the SiO2 substrate as a phase reference for accurate determination of the interfacial complex susceptibility. The obtained spectra revealed that the hydrogen atoms of the methyl group preferentially orient toward the air side (CH3-up configuration) at the air/DMSO interface, whereas they orient toward the bulk DMSO side (CH3-down configuration) at the SiO2/DMSO interface. Furthermore, introducing graphene, an optically transparent two-dimensional carbon material relevant to practical carbon electrodes, shifts the most probable configuration at the interface: the S=O bond points toward the liquid phase, while the methyl groups orient nearly perpendicular to the surface normal. MD simulations with polarizable models well reproduced the spectral band shapes and signs, revealing the physical meaning of the signs of imaginary amplitudes in terms of orientation and local solvation effects. These results provide molecular-level insights into how the substrate and graphene affect the interfacial structures and demonstrate HD-SFG spectroscopy, combined with polarizable MD simulations, as a powerful approach for elucidating molecular-level structures at buried electrochemical interfaces for energy storage systems.
relevance_reason: Applies classical/polarizable molecular dynamics simulations of explicit DMSO molecules at interfaces alongside HD-SFG, satisfying (a), (b), and (c) as an atomistic MD application.

title: EmbASI: An extensible Pythonic framework for DFT-in-DFT and WF-in-DFT embedding
abstract: High-level quantum mechanical (QM) simulations are important for understanding chemical and physical systems, but these methods scale unfavorably with system size, and this limits calculations to model representations of the real systems. To simulate realistic systems, approaches such as hierarchical quantum mechanics in quantum mechanics embedding (QM/QM) can be used to localize the accurate electronic structure methods to a region of chemical interest, with the wider environment represented using a less expensive embedding potential. However, implementing embedding procedures into established QM software packages is often challenging due to their monolithic design and complex software structure. Here, we present a modular and open-source approach that enables QM/QM embedding using established electronic structure codes with reduced development overhead. We demonstrate the new software, EmbASI, using the projection-based embedding theory scheme. Calculations performed for pentanol and organic dimers demonstrate the efficacy of the hierarchical density functional theory (DFT) embedding approach with the charge localization and partitioning procedures implemented in the wrapper environment; when using a truncated local atomic orbital basis, wavefunction-in-DFT embedding calculations demonstrate speed-ups of 32× for a 70 atom system, evaluated with RPA@PBE-in-PBE relative to a full RPA@PBE calculation, while introducing minimal errors to the total energies of the embedding simulations (−1). We then demonstrate capabilities for realistic extended zeolite models, achieving similar minimal errors with significant compute speed-up and memory reductions. The results demonstrate the capabilities of EmbASI for immediate applied QM/QM modeling and provide a broader foundation for multiscale QM simulations using established electronic structure infrastructure.
relevance_reason: Presents a DFT-in-DFT and WF-in-DFT embedding framework with explicit-atom calculations, satisfying (a), (b), and (c) as an electronic-structure/embedding method development.

title: Hydrogen sublattice in LaH$_{12}$: structural stability and possible ordering motifs
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06424v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Lanthanum polyhydrides, synthesized under extreme pressure, exhibit near-room-temperature superconductivity. Finding a precise arrangement of the hydrogen sublattice that is critical for understanding the strong electron-phonon coupling remains experimentally unresolved due to the small X-ray scattering form factor of hydrogen atoms. In this work, we attempt to computationally reconstruct hydrogen sublattices of the LaH$_{12}$ at 100-200 GPa combining unconstrained evolutionary searches and structure generation with fixed lanthanum sublattice. By implementing a similarity metric, we screen the computationally generated configurations against experimental powder X-ray diffraction data. We specifically identify the trigonal $R\bar{3}$-LaH$_{12}$ and pseudo-hexagonal $C222_1$-La$_2$H$_{24}$ phases, which demonstrate close agreement with the experimental X-ray diffraction data. First-principles calculations confirm the metallic and superconducting nature of these hydrides. Crucially, our lattice dynamics analysis using the stochastic self-consistent harmonic approximation (SSCHA) indicates that these structures are dynamically stable. We reveal the presence of molecular H$_2$ units and soft phonon modes in the trigonal LaH$_{12}$ that suppresses superconductivity ($T_c \ge 30$ K), while the hydrogen clathrate network in the $C222_1$ phase drives strong electron-phonon interactions, yielding the coupling parameters of $\lambda\approx 1.83$, $\omega_{\log} \approx 87.5$ meV and transition temperature of $T_c\approx 150$ K at 150 GPa.
relevance_reason: Combines evolutionary crystal structure prediction with fixed La sublattice, first-principles DFT relaxation, and SSCHA lattice-dynamics stability analysis on explicit atoms, satisfying (a), (b) DFT/geometry optimization and phonons, and (c) resolving the LaH12 hydrogen sublattice.

title: Brueckner Orbitals in Local Pair Natural Orbital Coupled-Cluster Theory: DLPNO-BCCD(T) and DLPNO-BCCD(T)_Lambda2
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06600v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this work, we implement closed-shell Brueckner orbitals for the efficient domain-based local pair natural orbital DLPNO-CCSD(T) and DLPNO-CCSD(T)$_{\Lambda}$ methods of the free and open-source \textsc{Psi4} package. We introduce a new algorithm that allows Brueckner orbitals to be computed within the DLPNO framework, resulting in the novel DLPNO-BCCD(T) and DLPNO-BCCD(T)$_{\Lambda_2}$ methods. We show that DLPNO-BCCD(T) approximates its canonical BCCD(T) counterpart with significantly lower errors relative to the errors incurred by DLPNO-CCSD(T) over CCSD(T). Through a test on the S22 set of noncovalent dimers, the peak error across the set is reduced from 0.36 kcal mol$^{-1}$ to 0.25 kcal mol$^{-1}$ using normal cutoffs, and 0.28 kcal mol$^{-1}$ to 0.13 kcal mol$^{-1}$ at tight cutoffs. In addition, we show that BCCD(T)$_{\Lambda_2}$, a ${\Lambda_2}$-only implementation of Brueckner orbitals for the asymmetric triples method, generally produces the best agreement with CCSDT, compared to the (T), (T)$_{\Lambda}$, and B(T) perturbative triples corrections. This is established through benchmarks on thermochemistry tests on the barrier heights of semibullvalene and bullvalene Cope rearrangement, while the robustness of DLPNO-BCCD(T)$_{\Lambda_2}$ is demonstrated along bond-breaking potential energy curves, where it matches the orbital-optimized quasi-variational asymmetric renormalized-triples OQVCCDAR(T) method closely for single-bond breaking, and approximates DLPNO-CCSDT respectably even when triple bonds are stretched, at a fraction of the computational cost.
relevance_reason: Implements Brueckner-orbital DLPNO-BCCD(T) and BCCD(T)_Lambda2 post-Hartree-Fock methods in Psi4 and benchmarks them on S22 dimers, barrier heights and bond-breaking curves, satisfying (a) explicit atomic/molecular systems, (b) post-HF method development, and (c) advancing the method's accuracy.

title: Sympathetic Cooling of Ionic Fullerenes with Ultracold Atoms to Millikelvin Temperatures
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05815v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Cooling complex molecular ions to millikelvin temperatures remains a major challenge because their intricate internal structures prevent laser cooling. Here, we propose to use an ultracold gas of Cd atoms to efficiently cool C$_{60}^+$ ions to average kinetic energies of approximately 20 mK, following an initial precooling stage with He buffer gas. Our approach is based on full molecular dynamics simulations using accurate ion-atom interaction potentials derived from high-level electronic structure methods. Furthermore, using a Monte Carlo approach, we predict the formation of C$_{60}^+$ Coulomb crystals supported solely by collisions with the buffer gas. The probability of reaching these cold states shows a pronounced dependence on the number of trapped ions, revealing the competition between neutral-atom cooling and many-ion dynamics in radio-frequency traps.
relevance_reason: Performs full molecular dynamics simulations of C60+ ions sympathetically cooled by ultracold Cd atoms using high-level electronic-structure-derived ion-atom potentials, plus Monte Carlo for Coulomb-crystal formation, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) classical MD/MC, and (c) an application study of a physical system.

title: Correlation-consistent Gaussian basis sets for copper solids from material-constrained atomic optimization
abstract:
arXiv:2607.11711v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Correlation-consistent Gaussian basis sets are central to systematic molecular quantum chemistry, but their direct use in periodic solids is often limited by severe linear dependence from diffuse atomically optimized primitives. This problem is particularly acute for metallic and metal-containing systems, where reliable complete-basis-set (CBS) extrapolation is needed for correlated-wavefunction benchmarks. We introduce material-constrained atomic optimization (MCAO), a basis-set optimization framework that preserves the atomic and correlation-consistent character of Gaussian basis sets while penalizing large overlap-matrix condition numbers in representative solids. As a proof of concept, we generate Dunning-style MCAO-cc-pVXZ basis sets (X = D, T, Q) for Cu with all-electron, scalar-relativistic all-electron, effective core potential (ECP), and pseudopotential treatments. The resulting basis sets remain numerically stable for Cu solids and surfaces while reproducing molecular Cu dimer energetics and plane-wave reference properties of bulk Cu. CBS-extrapolated random-phase approximation calculations further enable a controlled assessment of pseudopotential, relativistic, and basis-set errors in bulk Cu and CO adsorption on Cu(111), providing scalar-relativistic all-electron Gaussian-basis benchmarks for the CO adsorption puzzle.
relevance_reason: MCAO develops correlation-consistent Gaussian basis sets for periodic Cu solids with RPA/DFT benchmarks of bulk and CO/Cu(111) adsorption, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) post-HF/DFT electronic-structure methodology, and (c) method advance.

title: From 4D to 2D: Efficient computation of the electron correlation energies of atoms in molecular systems
abstract: The accurate modeling of (bio)molecular systems remains a major challenge in computational chemistry. In recent years, machine learning potentials (MLPs) have emerged as a promising approach, combining the efficiency of classical force fields with near quantum-mechanical accuracy. Among these, the physics-informed MLP FFLUX employs the Interacting Quantum Atoms (IQA) energy partitioning scheme to decompose molecular energies into atomic contributions derived from quantum mechanics for machine learning. However, incorporating two-electron correlation energies into IQA, and consequently into FFLUX, is currently unfeasible for larger systems en masse, due to the steep computational scaling associated with the necessary storage and evaluation of the two-particle density matrix (2PDM). In this work, we introduce a proof-of-concept workflow that employs density fitting (DF) to compress the 2PDM into a two-index representation, thereby accelerating the IQA partitioning of two-electron correlation energies. By expressing traditionally four-center electron repulsion integrals in terms of auxiliary basis functions, the DF approximation enables a size reduction of the 2PDM from O(N4) to O(NDF2), where N is the number of basis functions and NDF is the size of the auxiliary basis set. The method proposed here is demonstrated using coupled cluster singles and doubles densities. The resulting reduction in computational cost and memory requirements enables correlated IQA analyses for significantly larger systems than previously accessible. Thus, this development provides an important step toward incorporating explicit electron correlation and hence dispersion directly into FFLUX atomic ML models, thereby improving both their physical robustness and transferability. This advance will eliminate the need to artificially add empirical potentials, or a posteriori dispersion correction.
relevance_reason: Density-fitting workflow accelerates CCSD-based IQA two-electron correlation energies for the FFLUX MLP; explicit molecular atoms and post-HF/MLIP method development satisfy (a)-(c).

title: Machine Learning the Complete Active-Space Wavefunction Reconstruction
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06779v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials enable multireference-quality reaction dynamics but do not retain the electronic structure underlying the predicted energies and forces. Recovering this information by independently performing complete active space self-consistent field (CASSCF) calculations is both expensive and potentially inconsistent. We introduce the Complete Active-Space Wave Function Reconstruction (CAS-WR) model, which learns the geometry-dependent electronic structure from CASSCF data and reconstructs the CAS wave function without repeated orbital optimization. Combined with uncertainty-based active learning, CAS-WR is demonstrated for the Diels--Alder reaction and \ce{TiC+}-catalyzed C--H activation. The approach enables trajectory-resolved analysis of multiconfigurational electronic structure across reactive ensembles. Preliminary applications to excited-state proton transfer and transition-metal photocatalysis suggest that CAS-WR can provide a general route toward recovering electronic structure along complex ground- and excited-state reactive dynamics.
relevance_reason: The CAS-WR model is trained on CASSCF data to reconstruct multiconfigurational wave functions along reactive MD trajectories generated with MLIPs, so (a) explicit atoms, (b) MLIP/reaction dynamics plus electronic structure data, and (c) method advance for trajectory-resolved electronic structure are satisfied.

title: Drift-React: One-step Generation of Reaction Pathways via SE(3) Drifting Fields
abstract:
arXiv:2605.22990v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Mapping reaction pathways and transition states (TS) is fundamental to chemistry but computationally expensive at scale. The minimum energy pathway (MEP) dictates reaction rates and mechanisms, yet recovering it via electronic-structure methods requires thousands of costly force evaluations. Recent generative models accelerate TS identification but rely on iterative inference and only predict isolated saddle-point snapshots, missing the continuous reaction trajectory. We introduce Drift-React, an $\mathrm{SE}(3)$-equivariant generative framework that predicts complete reaction pathways in a single forward pass from only reactant and product geometries. By shifting distribution evolution to training via a Sinkhorn-weighted drifting field, Drift-React eliminates both the iterative force evaluations of NEB-style methods and the sequential ODE/SDE integration of diffusion and flow matching models. Evaluated on the Transition1x and Halo8 datasets, our one-step model generates physically consistent MEPs that accurately capture energetic bottlenecks and enable arbitrary-resolution sampling along the reaction coordinate. For isolated TS prediction, Drift-React matches the sub-{\AA}ngstr\"om accuracy of state-of-the-art iterative models while delivering orders-of-magnitude acceleration, clearing a major computational bottleneck for large-scale reaction network exploration.
relevance_reason: Drift-React is an SE(3)-equivariant generative model that outputs full 3D reaction pathways and transition states from reactant/product geometries and is validated energetically against MEP/TS references on Transition1x and Halo8, satisfying (a), (b) (TS/MEP methodology advance), and (c).

title: Anomalous thermal transport in isotope-enriched germanium carbide
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06663v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Advances in modern electronics demand the dissipation of heat fluxes approaching 1000 W cm$^{-2}$, which drives an urgent need for materials with thermal conductivity ($\kappa$) exceeding 1000 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$. Here, by solving the Boltzmann transport equation considering both three- and four-phonon interactions, we observe that isotopically pure cubic germanium carbide (GeC) exhibits a remarkable $\kappa$ of 1018 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ at room temperature, which is further corroborated by state-of-the-art machine-learning molecular dynamics simulations. Two unique mechanisms underlie this anomalously high $\kappa$: a remarkably strong isotopic enhancement effect (289%) and a surprisingly modest suppression due to four-phonon scattering (22%)-despite the presence of a wide acoustic-optical phonon gap. Moreover, we find that GeC defies the conventional Leibfried-Schlomann formula and exhibits a non-monotonic variation of $\kappa$ with external hydrostatic pressure at elevated temperatures. Our findings establish isotope-enriched GeC as a material of ultrahigh $\kappa$ and an ideal platform for exploring exotic phonon physics.
relevance_reason: Boltzmann transport with three-/four-phonon scattering corroborated by machine-learning interatomic potential molecular dynamics of explicit GeC structures, satisfying (a) atoms, (b) MLIP-driven MD, and (c) thermal transport application.

title: Open-shell Configuration State Functions as trial states for phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06790v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The accurate description of open-shell states in molecular systems poses challenges for approximate electronic structure methods. One emerging approach is to variationally optimize the orbitals of a single user-selected Configuration State Function (CSF), i.e., a linear combination of Slater determinants that is constructed as an eigenstate of the total spin operator. In this work we explore the use of these orbital-optimized single CSFs as trial wavefunctions in phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (ph-AFQMC), a stochastic method that recovers electron correlation by evolving an initial state in imaginary time, subject to a constraint imposed by the trial state. We investigate the symmetric stretch of H-He-H, a series of small $p$-block compounds with diradicaloid singlet states, twisted ethene conformers, and a bimetallic iron-sulfur complex. We find that accurate energetics are obtained for states dominated by open-shell character, and that for certain atoms and diatomics the accuracy can be significantly improved when the trial is made to also preserve the relevant angular momentum symmetries. Furthermore, our study reveals that the open-shell CSF trial is suboptimal when the target electronic state reflects a significant mixture of ionic and covalent character, e.g., at shorter bond lengths in H-He-H and for the superexchange-stabilized ground state of [2Fe-2S]$^{2+}$. Our findings suggest that ph-AFQMC using CSF trial states is a promising method for many (but not all) strongly correlated molecular states, especially given its relatively low computational cost, and that it provides a reasonable non-perturbative way to recover some of the dynamic correlation that is otherwise missing in the CSF.
relevance_reason: Benchmarks open-shell configuration-state-function trial states in phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo for H-He-H, diradicaloid singlets, twisted ethene and a [2Fe-2S] complex, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) post-HF-level stochastic electronic structure method, and (c) methodological development and accuracy assessment.

title: Atomic-Scale Phonon Engineering for Enhanced Thermal Transport in Wafer-Scale-Bonded $\beta$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC Heterostructures
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05810v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Bonding semiconductors to substrates with high thermal conductivity is a promising way to solve the heat-dissipation problem of materials that transport heat poorly, and it avoids the lattice-matching constraints of conventional epitaxy. However, the lattice mismatch remains, leaving the two materials with mismatched phonon states, while poor interface quality scatters phonons even more. Together, these effects block phonon transport across the bonded interface and make interfacial thermal resistance a critical bottleneck, calling for careful interface engineering. Here, $\beta$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC serves as a model system for a phonon-bridging strategy. A nanoscale crystalline Si interlayer is designed and fabricated by wafer bonding to bridge the mismatched phonon states of $\beta$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$ and SiC. Spatially resolved electron energy-loss spectroscopy and molecular dynamics simulations show that this Si layer opens new channels for phonon transport across the interface. The engineered interface raises the interfacial thermal conductance to 165 MW m$^{-2}$ K$^{-1}$ -- the highest value yet reported for $\beta$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC interfaces. These results offer an effective way to manage heat in $\beta$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$ devices and point to a general approach for building phonon-bridging interfaces that improve heat dissipation in heterogeneous systems.
relevance_reason: Uses classical molecular dynamics simulations to model phonon transport across a bonded β-Ga2O3/SiC interface with explicit atoms, satisfying (a) explicit atomistic representation, (b) molecular dynamics, and (c) application to understand interfacial thermal conductance.

title: Generating Physically Consistent Molecules with Energy-Based Models
abstract:
arXiv:2605.18381v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Molecules in equilibrium follow a Boltzmann distribution, making the underlying energy landscape a physically grounded modeling objective. However, such landscapes are difficult to learn from data and, once learned, hard to sample from. Diffusion and flow-matching models sidestep these difficulties by learning a time-conditional score or transport field between noise and data, losing the energy inductive bias in exchange for a more tractable training objective. We introduce EBMol, an energy-based model (EBM) that restores this inductive bias by learning an atom-additive scalar potential without explicit simulation during training. Our method employs a flow-inspired Restoring Field Matching objective to approximate the energy landscape. We adopt the Mirror-Langevin algorithm for sampling, enabling unified updates of atomic positions and types, and incorporate parallel tempering for inference-time compute scaling. EBMol is the first EBM for 3D molecular generation to achieve state-of-the-art performance on QM9 and GEOM-Drugs. Moreover, we show that the learned energy landscape serves as a principled quality metric for ranking and filtering configurations, and demonstrate controllable generation without retraining through shape-steered sampling via potential composition and zero-shot linker design.
relevance_reason: EBMol learns an atom-additive 3D energy potential and samples explicit atomic positions with Mirror-Langevin plus parallel tempering, so (a) explicit 3D atoms and (b) potential-based Langevin sampling are satisfied and (c) is a generative-model contribution validated energetically, but the emphasis is on generative ML rather than simulation methodology.

title: EnGOAT: An Energy–Geometry Analysis Toolkit for Free-Energy Surfaces of Mobile Species in Crystalline Materials
relevance_reason: EnGOAT analyzes energy–geometry free-energy surfaces for mobile species in crystals, i.e. NEB/energy-landscape workflows built on DFT or interatomic-potential calculations of explicit atoms, satisfying (a), (b) and (c).

title: Critical point search and linear response theory for computing electronic excitation energies of molecular systems. II. CASSCF
abstract: The computation of excited states within the Complete Active Space Self-Consistent Field (CASSCF) framework remains a significant challenge in quantum chemistry, both theoretically and algorithmically. In this work, we extend the Kähler manifold formalism introduced in Paper I Grazioli et al. [J. Chem. Phys. 164, 064101 (2026)] of this series to the CASSCF theory and draw a geometrical connection from the time-dependent CASSCF equations to state-specific and linear response methodologies for excited states. This is achieved by first investigating the underlying CASSCF manifold and identifying its Kähler structure, which is complicated by the nontrivial coupling of CI and orbital degrees of freedom. Building on these theoretical findings, we derive the CASSCF linear response equations in a straightforward manner and develop a robust state-specific method that relies solely on first-order derivatives of the CASSCF energy functional. Numerical results on representative molecular systems—water, formaldehyde, and ethylene—demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed state-specific method, while revealing the difficulty of reliable identification of excited states due to nonlinearity induced by the CASSCF theory.
relevance_reason: Develops CASSCF linear-response and state-specific excited-state methods with explicit molecular test systems, satisfying (a), (b), and (c) through quantum-chemistry method advance.

title: Neutral-to-zwitterionic transition in protonated glycine clusters drives magic number stability
abstract: Molecular clusters in the gas phase often exhibit “magic numbers,” corresponding to enhanced abundances at specific cluster sizes, typically attributed to particularly stable geometric arrangements. Here, we combine electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI-MS) with quantum chemical calculations to investigate the structure and stability of protonated glycine clusters. The experimental mass spectrum reveals pronounced magic numbers at cluster sizes n = 3 and n = 6. To elucidate their origin, we performed a systematic computational investigation of glycine clusters up to n = 7, including global structure searches, high-level electronic structure calculations, and thermal stability simulations. Our calculations show that clusters with n = 2, 4, and 5 are predominantly composed of canonical glycine molecules; the n = 7 clusters are composed of both neutral and zwitterionic glycine molecules, whereas the hexamer is the first cluster size for which fully zwitterionic structures become thermodynamically preferred. This neutral-to-zwitterionic transition gives rise to a highly cooperative hydrogen-bonding network and is accompanied by a pronounced increase in thermal stability, providing a natural explanation for the exceptional abundance of the hexamer. In contrast, the enhanced abundance of the trimer is consistent with kinetic stabilization under electrospray ion-source conditions rather than with the thermodynamic stability of its global free-energy minimum. These findings provide molecular-level insight into the emergence of magic numbers in glycine clusters and the onset of zwitterionic stabilization in finite molecular assemblies.
relevance_reason: Performs global structure searches, high-level quantum-chemical calculations, and thermal stability simulations on explicit protonated glycine clusters, satisfying (a), (b), and (c) as an atomistic application.
